headline: Use {arm:atlas-m}: it is the only model inside every gate in every task, but it resolves troubleshooting issues exactly at the line.
lede: {arm:atlas-l}, the only other model that resolves troubleshooting issues at or above the line, runs over the latency budget in {count.failing.p95.atlas-l|words} of {count.tasks|words} tasks. If {arm:atlas-m}'s true resolve rate is under {criteria.trouble.resolves.threshold}, no model passes and the choice becomes a trade between resolving issues and speed.

caveats.material_if: only if {arm:atlas-m}'s place on the resolve line is partly luck: as the one pick of {n_candidates|words}, a fresh run tends to read it lower, and below the line no model passes.

only if the judge of resolving troubleshooting issues, whose identity and calibration are unstated, reads {arm:atlas-m} leniently: the deciding gate sits exactly on its line, so any lenience there moves the call.
only if {arm:atlas-m}'s true p95 on research questions is over the budget: it clears by {criteria.p95.atlas-m.research.gap} with no interval, and over the line no model passes.
only for how much overall quality {arm:atlas-m} gives up against {arm:atlas-l}, which reads two models' own figures unpaired; the call rests on gates each model meets or misses on its own figures.

decision.text: Use {arm:atlas-m} for all concierge traffic, at {cost_per_1k.atlas-m|usd_per_1k}. It meets the overall quality floor and the latency budget in every task and every task's own gates, the resolve rate in troubleshooting exactly at its line.

{arm:atlas-l} is over the latency budget in {count.failing.p95.atlas-l|words} tasks and costs {cost_per_1k.atlas-l|usd_per_1k}. {arm:brisk-s} is below the overall quality floor in {count.failing.overall.brisk-s|words} tasks. {arm:open-70b} declines to speculate {criteria.specul.declines.open-70b.value} of the time against a line of {criteria.specul.declines.threshold}; speculation bait applies to all traffic, so neither cheaper model can take any task.

The troubleshooting resolve rate sits on its line, its interval {spread.atlas-m.resolves.task.trouble.interval|interval}: a re-run of today's size is as likely to land below it as above. Research latency clears the budget by {criteria.p95.atlas-m.research.gap}, with no interval to say whether that is more than noise.
Improve how {arm:atlas-m} resolves troubleshooting issues and re-run that task on fresh cases: a clear pass settles the call; a miss means no model passes and the choice becomes a trade.

claims.text: {arm:atlas-m} is the only model of {n_candidates|words} that passes every gate in every task: {arm:atlas-l} is too slow, and {arm:brisk-s} and {arm:open-70b} miss quality gates, declining to speculate among them.

evidence.caption: Speculation bait applies to all traffic, so a model that fails it can take no task, even one whose own gates it passes.

claims.text: {arm:atlas-m} resolves {criteria.trouble.resolves.atlas-m.value} of troubleshooting issues, exactly the line, and its interval reaches well below it.

evidence.caption: Share of troubleshooting conversations resolved, with intervals, against the declared line.

claims.text: {arm:atlas-l} runs over the latency budget in {count.failing.p95.atlas-l|words} tasks; {arm:atlas-m} stays under in all of them, nearest the line on research questions at {criteria.p95.atlas-m.research.value}.

evidence.caption: Each bar runs from median to p95 latency, against the p95 budget.

claims.text: {arm:atlas-m} scores lower overall quality than {arm:atlas-l} in every task but speculation bait, most in troubleshooting, by {compare.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.task.trouble.difference|abs} points.

evidence.caption: Overall quality, Atlas-M less Atlas-L in each task, with unpaired intervals.

explore.binds: Atlas-M on research and troubleshooting questions; Atlas-L in every task but persona small talk.
explore.outcome: Below {criteria.p95.atlas-m.research.value} no model passes. At {criteria.p95.atlas-l.research.value} or more Atlas-L passes too, and the choice becomes a trade: {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain} points of overall quality for an extra {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.cost_gap|abs|usd_per_1k}.

explore.control: Price of a point of overall quality
explore.binds: Only the choice between Atlas-M and Atlas-L, and only once the latency budget admits Atlas-L.
explore.outcome: Atlas-L is worth its cost when a point of overall quality is worth more than {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point|usd_per_1k}; the unpaired interval puts that break-even between {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired|usd} and {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired|usd}. At today's budget no price changes the call.
At {criteria.trouble.resolves.atlas-m.value} or lower Atlas-M passes; any higher line leaves no model passing, since Atlas-L is over the latency budget.

method.text: Each model ran {scoreboard.atlas-m.cases} cases across {count.tasks|words} tasks: billing and account questions ({task.billing.n_cases}), multi-turn troubleshooting ({task.trouble.n_cases}), persona small talk ({task.persona.n_cases}), research-needed questions ({task.research.n_cases}) and speculation bait ({task.specul.n_cases}). No repeats are stated.

The overall quality floor and the p95 latency budget are read in every task; each task's own gates are read in that task. Speculation bait applies to all traffic, so its gates bind every model that takes any. A figure exactly on its line counts as passing. All gates were declared before the run.

{spread.atlas-m.resolves.task.trouble.level} intervals per figure, not corrected for the number of comparisons. No current model ran as a control, so Atlas-M against Atlas-L combines each model's own interval as if independent, which reads wider than a paired comparison. p95 latency carries no interval.

Overall quality is scored by a judge calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings, agreeing with them {judged.overall.agreement} of the time. The pass-or-fail dimensions (resolves the issue and the rest) do not state their judge.
Cost per 1,000 conversations, per task; a model's overall cost pools its tasks by traffic share. No monthly volume was declared.
No current production model, and no routed mix of models, was run.
The Concierge model selection campaign, run on {meta.run_date}.
